title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
This is an operational envelope failure rather than a driving failure. The vehicles did not misread the road or collide with anything; they ran their batteries down while stationary in traffic that had stopped moving. The conditions the fleet met that day, heavy holiday volume, major traffic disruption and unexpected road closures, were outside what its energy planning appears to have allowed for, and the result was a dozen or more vehicles halted in place, some needing towing.

The failure sits in fleet operations and energy management, not in perception or route choice. Catching it would have required treating prolonged standstill as a foreseeable state rather than an edge case: modelling charge consumption at zero speed over long periods, monitoring state of charge across the fleet in real time, and having a way to pull vehicles out of a forming jam before they strand. The fire on one vehicle, which followed it driving over fireworks lying in the street, is a separate physical event from the battery drain.

What is not established is any finding that the driving system made a wrong decision, or any determination of what caused the fire. The account of traffic disruption and road closures is the company's own attribution, and the mayor's office announced discussions rather than conclusions. No investigation result or regulatory finding is reported here.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets on Saturday during Fourth of July celebrations when their batteries drained while stuck in heavy traffic following fireworks displays near the Golden Gate Bridge. Video verified by NBC News showed at least a dozen stationary Waymo vehicles, including Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up on streets, with some requiring towing. The company attributed the gridlock to major traffic disruptions, high traveler volume, and unexpected road closures. One vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks on the street, though no injuries were reported.

The incident prompted frustration from some motorists who waited nearly two hours in standstill traffic. Waymo said its roadside assistance team worked to clear the vehicles and that the company is evaluating how to strengthen its resilience during major traffic disruptions. Mayor Daniel Lurie's office announced plans to discuss the situation with public and private partners to improve future experiences. This incident follows a December outage when over 100,000 customers lost power and Waymo briefly paused service after some vehicles stalled at intersections with non-functioning traffic lights.
